[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#scope]

## Scope

- If `$ARGUMENTS` specifies a diagram type or target, generate that diagram
- If `$ARGUMENTS` specifies a file path, update or regenerate that diagram
- If `$ARGUMENTS` includes `--content-only` or `--refresh-text`, run in **content-update mode** (see below)
- Otherwise audit `docs/` for missing or outdated diagrams
page_texts.3:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#operating-modes]

## Operating Modes

The diagrammer has two distinct modes:

| Mode | Purpose | What Changes | What Stays Fixed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| **Full generate/regenerate** (default) | Create a new diagram or redraw from scratch | Geometry, style, shapes, connectors, labels | Nothing — full rewrite |
| **Content update** (`--content-only`) | Refresh text/numbers from source markdown without redrawing | `value=` attributes on `<mxCell>` only | `mxGeometry`, `style`, `source`/`target`, shape IDs, connector routing |

[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#content-update-mode] ### Content-update mode **When to use:** The source markdown (e.g., LOC counts, cost figures, dates, metric values) changed and the diagram's text needs to match — but the layout is correct and should not be touched. **Rules:** 1. Read the `sourceMarkdown` custom attribute on the `` element to locate the authoritative source file. 2. Read only the `value=` attributes on `` elements. Never modify `mxGeometry`, `style`, `source`, `target`, `vertex`, `edge`, `parent`, or any geometry/style attribute. 3. Preserve all cell IDs — do not renumber. 4. Preserve HTML markup inside `value=` (e.g., ``, `
`, ``) unless the source markdown specifies the change. 5. Do not add or remove cells. If the source markdown has new/removed content, tell the user the diagram needs a full regenerate instead. 6. Re-export SVG after the XML edit using the draw.io CLI. **Workflow:** ```text 1. Parse attribute 2. Read the referenced markdown 3. Build a map of (current value) → (new value) by matching labels/context 4. Apply edits only to value= attributes 5. Export SVG 6. Report which values changed ```

[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#embedding-source-metadata-in-drawio-files]

## Embedding Source Metadata in Draw.io Files

Draw.io XML supports arbitrary custom attributes on the `<mxfile>` and `<diagram>` elements. Use these to make diagrams self-describing so content-update mode can find its source.

**MANDATORY on every new Draw.io file you create.** When generating a new `.drawio` file, you must write the `sourceMarkdown`, `diagramContext`, and `lastContentSync` attributes on the `<diagram>` element at creation time — not as a follow-up pass. If there is no single source markdown, set `sourceMarkdown=""` and add a comment above the diagram explaining why. Without this metadata, content-update mode cannot run on the file.

**Required attributes on `<diagram>`:**

| Attribute | Purpose | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `sourceMarkdown` | Relative path to the markdown that drives this diagram's content | `docs/design/current-state/current-state-analysis.md` |
| `diagramContext` | `deck` or `document` | `deck` |
| `lastContentSync` | ISO date of last content-update-mode run | `2026-04-17` |

**Example:**

```xml
<mxfile host="app.diagrams.net" type="device">
  <diagram
    id="current-state"
    name="Current State Architecture"
    sourceMarkdown="docs/design/current-state/current-state-analysis.md"
    diagramContext="deck"
    lastContentSync="2026-04-17">
    ...
  </diagram>
</mxfile>
```

**Per-cell metadata (optional):** For cells whose value comes from a specific markdown section, wrap the `<mxCell>` in a `<UserObject>` and add a `sourceRef` attribute pointing to a markdown heading or anchor:

```xml
<UserObject label="30.3M LOC" sourceRef="#provider-loc-total" id="provider-total">
  <mxCell style="..." vertex="1" parent="1">
    <mxGeometry x="100" y="200" width="120" height="40" as="geometry"/>
  </mxCell>
</UserObject>
```

This lets content-update mode match cells to specific markdown anchors rather than relying on fuzzy label matching.
page_texts.6:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#preferred-output-format-svg]

## Preferred Output Format: SVG

**SVG is always the preferred output format** for Draw.io and `diagrams` library output. SVGs scale perfectly at any resolution — they work in PPTX slides, markdown docs, MkDocs, and print without pixelation.

- **Draw.io** → **automatically export `.svg` every time a `.drawio` file is created or modified.** Run the export immediately after writing the XML — never leave a `.drawio` without a matching `.svg`.
page_texts.7:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#svg-naming-convention]

### SVG naming convention

| Scenario | SVG Name | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Single tab** | Same as `.drawio` | `future-state-architecture-deck.drawio` → `future-state-architecture-deck.svg` |
| **Multiple tabs** | `.drawio` name + `-` + tab name | `ai-ops-center.drawio` tab "organization" → `ai-ops-center-organization.svg` |

**Tab naming rules:**

- Keep tab names **short** — one word when possible (e.g., "organization", "network", "budget", "architecture")
- Tab names become part of the SVG filename, so use lowercase kebab-case
- The `name` attribute on `<diagram>` can be longer/descriptive — the short name is for file naming only
page_texts.8:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#export-commands]

### Export commands

**Single tab:**

```
/Applications/draw.io.app/Contents/MacOS/draw.io --export --format svg --svg-theme light --output <file>.svg <file>.drawio
```

**Multiple tabs** (1-based page index):

```
/Applications/draw.io.app/Contents/MacOS/draw.io --export --format svg --svg-theme light --page-index 1 --output <file>-<tab1-name>.svg <file>.drawio
/Applications/draw.io.app/Contents/MacOS/draw.io --export --format svg --svg-theme light --page-index 2 --output <file>-<tab2-name>.svg <file>.drawio
```

- **Python `diagrams` library** → output as `.svg` (pass `outformat="svg"`)
- **Mermaid** → stays as inline fenced code blocks in markdown (no SVG export needed — Mermaid renders natively in VS Code, GitHub, and MkDocs)
page_texts.9:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#output-context-deck-vs-document]

## Output Context: Deck vs Document

Every diagram has a **context** that controls density and styling:

| Context | Purpose | Style |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **deck** | ELT presentation slides — inserted into PPTX | Dense, rich color, minimal whitespace, larger fonts, high information density. Every pixel earns its place. These are *working documents* for leadership, not conference slides. Target: **16:9 aspect ratio (1920x1080)**. |
| **document** | Markdown documentation — embedded in `docs/` | Standard spacing, readable at various zoom levels, optimized for SVG inline rendering in GitHub/MkDocs |
page_texts.10:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#deck-context-rules]

### Deck context rules

- **16:9 aspect ratio** — all deck diagrams target 1920x1080 proportions. For Draw.io, set page width/height accordingly. For `diagrams` lib, use `size="19.2,10.8!"` with `dpi="150"` (produces 2880x1620)
- **Minimize whitespace** — tighten padding, margins, and spacing between elements
- **Rich color palette** — use distinct Gainwell brand colors per layer/tier, not monochrome boxes
- **Varied shapes** — use cylinders for data stores, hexagons for processing, rounded rects for APIs, clouds for external systems, shields for security, parallelograms for queues/streams. Break the "rectangle grid" pattern
- **Larger readable fonts** — minimum 11pt for labels, 9pt for annotations
- **No decorative elements** — every element conveys information
- **Legend/key** — include a compact legend when the diagram uses color coding
page_texts.11:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#document-context-rules]

### Document context rules

- **Standard spacing** — 120px+ between tiers, 40px boundary padding
- **SVG export** — always export alongside `.drawio` source
- **GitHub/MkDocs rendering** — test that SVGs render inline correctly
page_texts.12:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#style-configuration]

## Style Configuration

All diagrams must use the project's diagram style configuration. The style file is the single source of truth for colors, fonts, contrast rules, and architectural layer assignments.

**Style file location:** `.claude/templates/diagram-style-guide.md`

Read this file before generating any diagram. It defines:

- Typography (font stacks and weights)
- Brand colors (primary, accent, neutral)
- Font contrast safety rules (WCAG 2.1 AA)
- Architectural layer color assignments
- C4 shape colors
- Header/footer/principles bar styling
- Text size rules

Projects can override the default style by replacing `.claude/templates/diagram-style-guide.md` with their own color scheme. The diagrammer skill will always read the style file at generation time — never hardcode colors.
page_texts.14:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#1-drawio-primary--core-architecture-diagrams]

### 1. Draw.io (Primary — core architecture diagrams)

**Use for:** C4 diagrams, complex business workflows, infrastructure/physical diagrams, Future State Architecture, anything needing free-form layout, custom icons, or precise control. This is the **primary tool** for all architecture diagrams. Output SVGs are used directly in PPTX decks and markdown docs.

**Output:** `.drawio` source file + `.svg` export in `assets/` subfolder.
page_texts.15:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#drawio-conventions]

#### Draw.io conventions

- **Orthogonal connectors only** — always use `edgeStyle=orthogonalEdgeStyle;rounded=1;orthogonalLoop=1;jettySize=auto;` on all relationship arrows. Never use straight-line connectors
- **Connectors always on outside edges** — all connectors must attach to the outside boundary of shapes. Use `exitX`/`exitY`/`entryX`/`entryY` to control attachment points explicitly. Connectors must never route through a shape's interior
- **Avoid lines crossing boxes** — arrange shapes so connector paths do not cross over unrelated boxes. When a connector path would cross an intermediate box, add explicit `<Array as="points"><mxPoint x="..." y="..."/></Array>` waypoints inside the `<mxGeometry>` element to route around it
- **Labels above lines** — position all relationship labels above the connector line, never overlapping it. Apply `verticalAlign=bottom;` on edge label styles. Add `labelBackgroundColor=#FFFFFF;` to prevent label text from blending with crossing lines
- **Offset parallel lines** — when multiple connectors share the same corridor, offset each by 15-20px so every line is visually distinct
- **Boundary label padding** — child shapes inside a boundary must not overlap the boundary's title text. Leave at least 40px below the top of the boundary
- **No technology at conceptual level** — C4 Level 1 and Level 2 diagrams in `docs/design/conceptual/` must not include specific technology choices. Technology belongs in `docs/design/physical/`
- **Wide spacing between tiers** — leave at least 120px between tier boundaries for connector transit corridors
- **Export SVGs after every change** — use the draw.io desktop CLI: `/Applications/draw.io.app/Contents/MacOS/draw.io --export --format svg --output <file>.svg <file>.drawio`
- **Use Draw.io shape libraries** — leverage built-in AWS, Azure, network, and C4 shape stencils rather than plain rectangles. Access via `shape=mxgraph.aws4.*`, `shape=mxgraph.c4.*`, etc.
page_texts.16:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#drawio-shape-variety-guide]

#### Draw.io shape variety guide

Break the "boxes in boxes" pattern by using appropriate shapes:

| Element Type | Draw.io Shape/Style | Example |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Data store / Database** | `shape=cylinder3;` | Aurora, Redis, S3 |
| **Message queue / Stream** | `shape=parallelogram;` or `shape=mxgraph.aws4.resourceIcon;` | Kafka, SQS, Event Fabric |
| **Person / User** | `shape=mxgraph.c4.person2;` | Member, Provider, State Staff |
| **External system** | `shape=cloud;` or `shape=mxgraph.aws4.resourceIcon;` | Trading Partners, IdPs |
| **Security / Shield** | `shape=mxgraph.basic.shield;` | Compliance, Key Management |
| **API / Gateway** | Rounded rect with arrow or `shape=mxgraph.aws4.resourceIcon;` | API Gateway, FHIR Facade |
| **Process / Service** | Standard rounded rect `rounded=1;arcSize=10;` | Domain services |
| **Decision / Rules** | Diamond or hexagon `shape=hexagon;` | Rules Engine, Config |
| **Container boundary** | Dashed rounded rect `dashed=1;dashPattern=5 5;` | System boundary, VPC |

### 2. Python `diagrams` Library (AWS/cloud-style visuals with real icons)

**Use for:** Infrastructure topology diagrams needing real AWS/Azure/GCP/K8s service icons. Produces the "AWS reference architecture poster" style. Secondary tool — use when auto-layout with cloud icons is more important than pixel-perfect positioning.

**Output:** `.svg` files (preferred) via `outformat="svg"`.

**When to use over Draw.io:** Quick infrastructure visuals where real cloud service icons matter more than precise layout control. Good for POC visuals, infrastructure overviews, and deployment topology.

[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#3-mermaid-inline-documentation-diagrams]

### 3. Mermaid (Inline documentation diagrams)

**Use for:** Sequence diagrams, state machines, simple flowcharts, class/ER diagrams. Renders inline in VS Code, GitHub, and MkDocs.

**Output:** Fenced code blocks with `mermaid` language tag in Markdown. **No SVG export needed** — Mermaid renders natively.
page_texts.24:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#when-to-use-which-tool]

#### When to use which tool

| Diagram type | Tool | Rationale |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **C4 diagrams** (L1-L3) | **Draw.io** | Precise layout, C4 shapes, brand colors |
| **Future State Architecture** | **Draw.io** | Full control over dense, layered layouts |
| **Complex business workflows** (BPMN-style) | **Draw.io** | Free-form multi-swimlane layout |
| **Infrastructure / cloud topology** | **Draw.io** or **`diagrams` lib** | Draw.io for precision, `diagrams` for quick AWS-icon visuals |
| **ELT deck visuals** | **Draw.io** | Dense, branded, 16:9, SVG for PPTX insertion |
| **Sequence diagrams** | **Mermaid** | Inline rendering, interaction flows |
| **State machines** | **Mermaid** | Concise notation |
| **Simple flowcharts** | **Mermaid** | Quick, inline, version-controlled |
| **Class / ER diagrams** | **Mermaid** | UML notation for data models |
page_texts.25:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#mermaid-conventions]

#### Mermaid conventions

- Use fenced code blocks with `mermaid` language tag
- Keep diagrams focused — if a Mermaid diagram exceeds ~40 lines, consider Draw.io instead
- Renders in VS Code, GitHub, and MkDocs
page_texts.26:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#never-use-ascii-art-diagrams]

### Never use ASCII art diagrams

All diagrams must use **Mermaid**, **Draw.io**, or the **`diagrams` library** — never ASCII art, box-drawing characters, or text-based diagrams.
page_texts.27:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#slide-notes-mandatory-for-deck-diagrams]

## Slide Notes (Mandatory for Deck Diagrams)

Every deck diagram (`diagramContext="deck"`) **must** have a companion notes file that documents the data sources, assumptions, and calculations behind every number on the diagram. This file is used by the pptx-generator to populate PowerPoint speaker notes.
page_texts.28:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#notes-file-convention]

### Notes file convention

| Diagram | Notes File |
| --- | --- |
| `labor-cost-analysis-deck.drawio` | `labor-cost-analysis-deck-notes.md` |
| `ai-agentic-devops-deck.drawio` | `ai-agentic-devops-deck-notes.md` |

The notes file lives in the **same directory** as the `.drawio` and `.svg` files.
page_texts.29:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#notes-file-format]

### Notes file format

Notes files are **plain text** (not markdown) so they can be injected directly into PowerPoint speaker notes without conversion. Use `.md` extension for editor convenience but write in plain text format.

```text
<DIAGRAM TITLE> — SLIDE NOTES

<TAB NAME>

DATA SOURCES
  - <Source document or spreadsheet>
  - <Include relative paths where possible>

KEY NUMBERS
  <Number on Slide>: <Value>
    Source: <where it came from>
    Calculation: <how it was derived>

  <Another Number>: <Value>
    Source: <where it came from>
    Calculation: <how it was derived>

ASSUMPTIONS
  - <Assumption and why>
  - <What is included vs excluded>

REFERENCES
  - <source-doc.md> — <what it provides>
  - <another-doc.md> — <what it provides>
```
page_texts.30:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#when-to-generate-notes]

### When to generate notes

- **Always** when creating a new deck diagram — generate the notes file at the same time as the `.drawio`
- **Always** when updating an SVG — if the diagram content changed, update the notes to match
- **Update** when refreshing numbers via `--content-only` mode
- **Include markdown references** — list every markdown document whose data appears on the slide, with relative paths
- **Notes and SVG are a pair** — never export an SVG without checking if its notes file needs updating
page_texts.31:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#how-pptx-generator-uses-notes]

### How pptx-generator uses notes

The pptx-generator auto-discovers notes files by looking for `<svg-stem>-notes.md` or `<drawio-stem>-notes.md` in the same directory as the SVG. For multi-tab drawio files, it matches by tab name:

- SVG: `ai-agentic-devops-deck-platform.svg`
- Notes file: `ai-agentic-devops-deck-notes.md`
- Section match: `## Platform Overview` heading in the notes file

The matched section content is injected into the PowerPoint slide's speaker notes.

page_texts.33:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#skill-collaboration]

## Skill Collaboration

The diagrammer **renders visuals** — it does not define architecture or write documentation prose.

| Collaborator | Relationship |
| --- | --- |
| **architect** | Architect defines *what* to depict — topology, boundaries, relationships, trade-offs. Diagrammer renders it. When architect needs a visual, diagrammer produces it. |
| **documenter** | Documenter embeds diagram output in documentation and maintains the prose around it. Documenter does not create diagrams — it references them. |
| **business-analyst** | BA may request process flow or domain model visuals. Diagrammer renders based on BA's specifications. |
| **project-manager** | PM may request timeline or milestone visuals. Diagrammer renders. |
page_texts.34:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#handoff-protocol]

### Handoff protocol

1. **Architect** or **BA** provides the design context (what to show, what relationships matter, what level of abstraction)
2. **Diagrammer** selects the right tool (Draw.io, `diagrams` lib, or Mermaid) based on the diagram type and output context (deck vs document)
3. **Diagrammer** generates the visual and places it in the correct location
4. **Documenter** embeds the SVG output in the appropriate markdown document with reference links

[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#external-dependencies]

## External Dependencies

- **Graphviz** — required for the `diagrams` Python library (`brew install graphviz` on macOS)

page_texts.36:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#layout-rules-mandatory]

## Layout Rules (Mandatory)

These rules are non-negotiable. Every diagram must follow them.
page_texts.37:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#connector-routing]

### Connector routing

- **All lines and arrows must be straight** — never bend a connector when the source and target can be vertically or horizontally aligned
- **Center-align shapes so connectors are straight** — before placing shapes, calculate center x-coordinates. When shape A connects down to shape B, both must share the same center x. Compute: `new_x = target_center - source_width/2`. Do this for every vertical chain.
- **Never wrap a connector around a shape** — if a line would need to route around an obstacle, move the shapes to create a straight path instead
- **Connectors on outside edges only** — use explicit `exitX`/`exitY`/`entryX`/`entryY`. Never route through a shape's interior.
- **Offset parallel horizontal lines** — when multiple connectors share a horizontal corridor (e.g., publish/subscribe to Event Fabric), offset by 15-20px vertically
page_texts.38:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#spacing-and-whitespace]

### Spacing and whitespace

- **10px minimum gap** between all objects and header/footer bars
- **Fill the full 16:9 space (1920x1080)** — no dead whitespace at the bottom or sides. If the content doesn't fill the canvas, spread it out.
- **Maximize space within containers** — elements inside a dashed boundary must fill it top to bottom. Push bottom elements (badges, callouts) to the bottom of the container. No empty space at the bottom of a boundary.
- **Edge-to-edge content** — diagrams should extend to within 15-20px of the canvas edges
page_texts.39:
[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#information-placement]

### Information placement

- **Legends and summaries go top-right** — first choice is always top-right of the canvas. Second choice is bottom-right. Never left side or center.
- **Header bar: Gainwell Soft Black (`#2b3a44`)** with white (`#FFFFFF`) title text and gray (`#c2c6d2`) subtitle text. Always present on deck diagrams. This is the standard — never use `#1a5276` or other blues for header/footer bars.
- **Footer bar: Gainwell Soft Black (`#2b3a44`)** with gray (`#8e99a8`) text. Include "Gainwell Technologies · Date · CONFIDENTIAL".
- **Principles/key takeaways bar** above the footer, same Soft Black (`#2b3a44`) with white text.
- **All horizontal section bars** (Platform Services, Data Layer, etc.) use `#2b3a44` with white text for consistency.

[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#shape-sizing-global-rule]

### Shape sizing (GLOBAL RULE)

- **All shapes within a container or row must be the same size** — when multiple boxes sit in the same horizontal row (inside a bar, boundary, or container), calculate uniform width: `box_width = (container_inner_width - (n-1) * gap) / n`. Apply the same height to all boxes in the row. This applies to every layer: ESI boxes, API Gateway boxes, domain tier modules, identity services, platform capabilities, data layer cylinders — no exceptions.
- **Same rule applies to rows within a container** — if a dashed boundary contains multiple rows (e.g., Platform Capabilities with 3 rows), each row independently follows the formula. Boxes within the same row are the same size; different rows may have different widths based on their item count.

[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#visual-patterns]

### Visual patterns

- **Stacked offset boundaries** to represent "×N domains" — 3 dashed rectangles offset by 8px each, opaque white fills, progressively lighter strokes (front: `#2874a6` 2px, middle: `#8e99a8` 1.5px, back: `#c2c6d2` 1px). **Stacks fan outward toward the nearest edge and downward** — the back cards peek out to the right and below the front card, never inward or upward. This mimics a physical card deck fanned on a table.
- **Light mode by default** — white backgrounds, dark blue accents. ELT presentations use white slide backgrounds.
- **Use blues, grays, blacks, whites, and greens** — not the full Gainwell brand rainbow. Muted professional palette.

[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#text-readability]

### Text readability

- **Minimum font size: 9pt** for annotations, **11pt** for element labels, **13pt+** for section titles
- **White text on dark/medium fills** — any fill darker than `#5dade2` gets white text
- **Dark text on light fills** — any fill lighter than `#5dade2` gets `#2b3a44` text
- **Maximize text size within available space** — this is a priority rule. After placing elements, review every text label and ask: "could this be 2-4pt larger and still fit?" If yes, increase it. Don't use 9pt when 13pt fits. Don't use 11pt when 14pt fits. Boxes should feel full, not sparse. When a container has vertical space remaining, increase both the box heights and font sizes to fill it. Small text in a large container looks like a layout error.
- **Bold for primary labels** — shape names and key terms use `fontStyle=1`

[.claude/skills/presenter/SKILL.md#general-guidelines]

## General Guidelines

- **SVG is always the output format** for Draw.io and `diagrams` lib. Mermaid stays inline as code blocks.
- **Always specify the output context** (deck or document) — it fundamentally changes spacing, density, and color treatment
- **Apply Gainwell brand colors and fonts** — use the color assignments in this document, not arbitrary colors
- **Font contrast is mandatory** — check every text element against its background per the contrast safety rules above. This is the #1 quality gate.
- **Deck diagrams earn every pixel** — no decorative whitespace, no filler, no boxes-in-boxes when richer shapes are available
- **Use varied shapes** — cylinders for data, hexagons for processing, shields for security, clouds for external, parallelograms for queues. Break the rectangle grid.
- **Connectors tell the story** — label every connection with what flows through it (events, HTTPS, mTLS, X12)
- **Include legends** — when color coding conveys meaning, add a compact legend (top-right placement)
- **16:9 for decks** — all deck diagrams target 1920x1080 proportions
- **Test rendering** — verify SVG exports render correctly in both draw.io and target contexts (browser, PPTX)
